answer: Each live identity must keep extending a verifiable delay chain seeded by a registration relic that is bound to one key and cannot be copied. Every epoch the agent publishes the newest proof, and the delay setting may not sit below a published nadir; a missed beat or a reused seed evicts the key and burns the deposit. Proofs are collected in a public lagoon so peers can re-run a random sample. A VDF is strictly sequential, so forged voters cannot share one core or one chain: each extra identity demands its own continuous delay work plus its own at-risk deposit.
